Official BPR-max uses activated positive score r+ and negative scores rj: wj=exp(rj)/Σk exp(rk), ℓ=−log[Σj wj·sigmoid(r+−rj)+1e−24]+λΣj wj·rj². λ is `bpreg`; this penalizes negative scores, distinct from parameter weight decay. Gradients flow through the softmax weights. The positive diagonal is excluded from weighting. Original Theano and official PyTorch sum per-example losses, then divide by configured batch size; there is no additional division by negative count. Original plain BPR instead sums pairwise negative log-sigmoids, including a constant diagonal term, so its scale increases with pool size. [Theano source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec/master/gru4rec.py), [PyTorch source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official/master/gru4rec_pytorch.py).

BPR-max supports linear or ELU scores; ELUα(x)=x for x≥0, α(exp(x)−1) otherwise. Official PyTorch applies ELU when `elu_param>0`, otherwise linear. Sampling combines other minibatch targets with `n_sample` additional draws shared across rows, drawn with replacement from q(i)∝training-frequency(i)^`sample_alpha` (0 uniform, 1 popularity). Duplicates and target collisions remain; only the designated positive diagonal is masked, with no history filtering. [Official implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official/master/gru4rec_pytorch.py).

For controlled comparisons, replay identical training examples and negative-ID tensors using a sampler RNG independent of model randomness; fix initialization, activation, optimizer, updates and masking. Compare baseline versus BPR-max at λ=0 first. Separately vary negative count using prefixes of one maximum-size pool, keeping batch size fixed; normalize plain BPR across negatives to avoid count-dependent scaling, explicitly documenting this departure from official reduction. Sweep λ on fixed pools; optionally apply the same score penalty to both objectives. Keep one model/category, seed 42, and select by fixed macro validation HR@10.
